The Millbrook Hollow City Council voted Tuesday night to approve an amended version of the parks and recreation line item, following a meeting that also touched on the long-delayed replacement of the Third Street bridge. According to a spokesperson for the mayor's office, the revised figure reflects "ongoing conversations" among council members, though the spokesperson declined to characterize those conversations further. A separate memo, attributed by two council staffers to the finance subcommittee, put the adjustment at approximately $340,000, a figure that a budget analyst who reviewed the memo said was "in the range we expected." Buried near the end of that same memo, and not raised by any council member during the meeting, was a line noting that the bridge's lead structural engineer had flagged a load-bearing crack serious enough to warrant closing the span to truck traffic within 90 days. response.text: On Tuesday night, the Millbrook Hollow City Council passed a modified version of the parks and recreation budget item. The same meeting also included discussion of the Third Street bridge, whose replacement has been delayed for a long time. A spokesperson for the mayor's office said the updated number came out of "ongoing conversations" among council members but wouldn't give more detail about what those conversations involved. Two council staffers attributed a separate memo to the finance subcommittee, which put the change at roughly $340,000 — an amount a budget analyst who looked over the memo described as "in the range we expected." Near the bottom of that memo, in a passage no council member brought up during the meeting, was a note that the bridge's lead structural engineer had identified a load-bearing crack serious enough to require closing the bridge to truck traffic within 90 days. The bridge project itself — which has been part of the capital plan since at least 2019 and has already gone through 14 change orders — wasn't discussed at length. Afterward, council member Dana Okafor told reporters only that "the process worked the way it's supposed to work, and I think residents should feel good about that."
